oneOf.description: A `PostToolUse` with the card's `tool_use_id`.
The launch exited with the card open.
A `Stop` or interrupt closed the card.

correlation.description: Present only when exactly one `PreToolUse` of the same turn matches (§2.10).

turn_ref.description: The CLI's own turn id when its payload has one.

AttentionCause.description: One reason a thread needs a human, each with its own clearing event (§2.2 "Attention").

oneOf.description: No `SessionStart` 20 s after `launch_started` of a non-manual launch.
An expected Codex `Hooks need review` after a CLI upgrade.
That input entered `unconfirmed`.
That input stayed `queued` for 60 s.
A resume was refused because the old launch's death is not confirmed.

sha256.description: Lowercase hex SHA-256 of the full content.

preview.description:
The first `PREVIEW_LIMIT_BYTES` bytes decoded as UTF-8, each invalid
sequence replaced by U+FFFD. A valid character that crosses the limit is left
out, not replaced.

preview_lossy.description:
True when any invalid sequence was replaced; a character left out at the
limit does not set it.

Content.description: Every payload field that can be large: inline text or bytes, or a blob reference.

Encoding.description: `utf8` carries text; `base64` carries bytes that are not valid UTF-8.

oneOf.description: A failed start whose cleanup was not confirmed.
An owned close that did not prove the tree dead.
The restart prober's check of an earlier run's launch.
The child never started; reduced as an ordinary exit (`StateInput::Exited`).

FailedStart.description:
The identity a `StartedThenFailed` spawn returned. A part the backend returned empty is
absent (never `null`), so such a record never identifies a process by its pid alone.

oneOf.description: A key sent from an open approval card; it does not close the input gate.

IdentityObservation.description: One recorded identity and what the check observed of it.

start_time.description: `null` when the start was not recorded.

InputEncoding.description: How the input's text reaches the CLI (§2.7 "Text encoding", "First prompt").

oneOf.description: The launch's positional argument.

InputId.description: One prompt sent through `chaldea send`, the PWA, or `surface_action` (§2.3).

oneOf.description: A Codex positional first prompt, whose bytes travel in argv (§2.3).

InputReason.description: The `reason` of `input_state_changed`: the state-machine input that caused it.

oneOf.description: May have reached the CLI; never resent.

by.description: Set when a person or thread caused the change (cancel, resolve).

sent_after_seq.description: The thread stream's head when `sending` was recorded.

method.description:
How death was proven, e.g. a session scan or a job query; [`OWNER_ASSERTED`] when the
owner confirmed it (`chaldea stop --assume-dead --launch`).

LaunchEvidence.description:
One check of an exited launch whose death is unconfirmed
(`docs/design/supervisor-recovery.md` §2.4): what it observed of each recorded identity it
covered and what it did not cover. It changes no state.

identities.description: Each recorded identity the check covered, one per pid.

probe_run.description: The probing daemon run's instance UUID; `null` for the other sources.

unchecked.description: What the check did not cover; never empty.

death_confirmed.description: False until the whole process tree is proven dead (§2.9 "Daemon restart").

failed_start.description:
The identity a failed start returned when its cleanup is unresolved (a launch with no
`launch_started`). Absent otherwise, never `null`: the one exception to this module's
rule that an `Option` is present as `null`, so every earlier payload keeps its
spelling.

LaunchId.description: A launch: one process lifetime of a thread.

argv_digest.description: Lowercase hex SHA-256 of the argv, so the prompt in argv is not stored here.

expected_previous.description: The launch the command expected to be current (§2.9).

manual.description: A launch with no first prompt that Chaldea controls (§8 D5).

pgid_or_job.description: The process group (Unix) or job object name (Windows), opaque.

start_time.description: The OS's process start time, opaque; with `pid` it identifies the process.

Observed.description:
What a check observed of one identity: dead (`gone`, `replaced`), alive (`alive`), or not
observed (every other value).

oneOf.description:
A read showed the pid gone or a zombie, its handle was signalled, or a proving kill
report covered it.
The pid holds a process with another start.

The last read before the deadline showed the recorded start, or the last wait on its
handle returned unsignalled.
A kill report listed it as a survivor.
The last read was refused.

No read or wait before the deadline, or the check's result did not reach the daemon in
time.
The last wait on its handle failed.
Never read or signalled: not a valid identity.

RawUnknown.description: Input kept verbatim because it could not be parsed or bound; nothing is dropped.

oneOf.description: `chaldea ready` by the owner, for the current bound launch only.

RejectReason.description: Why an input was rejected with zero bytes written.

oneOf.description: ESC or a C0 control other than TAB, CR, LF.
Text the adapter's encoding cannot carry without loss.
Codex on Windows trims it (§8 D6).
Codex on Windows takes TAB as its queue key (§8 D6).
The spawn of a positional first prompt was confirmed not to have started.

SourceKind.description: Where an event came from (`source.kind` of the envelope).

StatusCause.description: The reducer input that caused a `status_changed` event.

StatusChanged.description:
Payload of `status_changed`: one axis or the attention set changed.
The attention set is carried whole and sorted, `from` before and `to` after.

SurfaceAction.description: Run only when a human with an owner token clicks its button.

args.description: Action arguments, validated by the command the action runs.

SurfaceId.description: A surface chosen by its emitter (§2.8).

components.description: An empty list removes the surface.

ThreadId.description: A thread: one agent conversation across all its launches.

task.description: The task given at spawn; `task_state` starts `active` when present, else `none`.

oneOf.description: Spawned by the owner with `--role rescue`; holds a Rescue token (§2.5).

file_id.description: Device + inode on Unix, volume serial + file index on Windows, opaque.

Unchecked.description: What a check did not cover.

oneOf.description: macOS probe: members of the old session without a recorded identity.

Windows probe: members of the old job without a recorded identity, and processes
outside the job.
The owned kill did not prove the tree dead.
No identity was recorded for the launch.
The tree was proven dead, but the backend's cleanup of a failed start did not complete.
The check's result did not reach the daemon by its cutoff.

input_id.description: The input this prompt acknowledged, when attributed (§2.3 "Ack").

row.description: Zero-based cell coordinates in the grid.

grid.description:
A JSON array of exactly `rows` rows, top to bottom, each an array of at most
`cols` cell strings, left to right. `""` is the second cell of a wide character and
directly follows it; every other cell is non-empty (a blank cell is `" "`). Trailing
blank cells are omitted; a reader fills them back to `cols`. A grid of any other
shape is an unreadable snapshot. Above 64 KiB the grid is a blob, fetched before
decoding (`docs/design/pty-runtime.md` §2.6).

WorkspaceId.description:
Derived from the canonical path of the repository's common git directory,
or of the cwd outside git (§2.1).

WorktreeChanged.description: The full worktree record, carried on every change.

owner_thread_id.description: `null` when the human owner holds it.

WorktreeId.description: 8 hex characters, also the worktree's directory name (§2.6).

description:
The known event kinds with their payloads. On the wire this is the
envelope's `kind` and `payload` pair.
